Experimental verification The experimental arrangement to verify Hooke’s law has been shown in the figure below. Two wires, one being a test wire and the other as a reference wire, are taken and suspended from a rigid support, hanging vertically. A Vernier apparatus is set up on the wires so that the extension on the test wire with respect to the reference wire is easily readable.
Fig 8.3: Hook’s Law verification
Loads are added in steps to a test wire, and the resulting extensions are noted at regular
intervals. This process is conducted within the elastic limit. After removing the weights,
contractions are noted. Finally, the extensions produced by the loads are calculated.
Experimentally, it is found that the extension produced is proportional to the applied load.

area Or, F = Nm-2 and (ML-1T-2) A Stress and pressure are both terms used in physics and engineering to describe the distribution of force within a material, but they refer to slightly different concepts:
Physics, Grade 11 | 187

Stress is a measure of the internal force per unit area acting within a material that arises from external forces applied to the material, such as stretching, compressing, shearing, or bending, and is a vector quantity. Pressure is a measure of the force per unit area applied on a surface, typically exerted by a fluid (liquid or gas), and is a vector quantity. Types of Stress: On the basis of the nature of the applied force, the stress developed is categorized as follows:
1) Normal stress: The force applied is normal to the surface. The normal stress is further divided as follows:

Fig 8.4: Normal stress i) Tensile stress: If the normal stress acts in the direction of the length and there is an increase in length, it is the tensile stress. ii) Compression stress: If the normal stress acts in the direction of the length and there is a decrease in length, it is compression stress.
2) Tangential (shearing) stress: When the force applied is parallel to the surface keeping the lower surface fixed, it is called tangential stress.
